mainTopic: Proper conduct and bodily concerns during תפלה, and the cleanliness and covering needed for קריאת שמע
overview: This amud starts by finishing a report about how רבי behaved while praying. A ברייתא seems to condemn that behavior: burping, yawning, sneezing and spitting during תפלה. The גמרא answers each point. רבי burped and yawned only when he couldn't help it, he sneezed from the nose (a good sign, says רב זירא), and he absorbed his spit discreetly, as רב יהודה teaches. רב הונא then limits the ban on praying aloud: it is allowed for someone who can't concentrate quietly, but only when praying alone. A story about רבי אבא brings the rule for someone who passes wind during תפלה. The גמרא next turns to קריאת שמע. It discusses a person covered by his garment in bed, and a person walking through filthy alleys, where רב הונא allows reciting with a covered mouth and רב חסדא strongly forbids it. ברייתות support each side, and פסוקים describe the one who keeps reciting in filth and the one who stops. The amud ends with רב הונא's ruling that a garment tied around the waist is enough covering to say שמע.

steps.title: The end of the report about רבי's conduct during prayer
steps.stepSummary: The report finishes describing what רבי did and did not do during תפלה: he felt his clothing, did not wrap himself, and covered his mouth when yawning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he would feel around in his garment, but he would not wrap himself. And when he yawned, he would put his hand on his chin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a report about what רבי did while he was praying. This report is the set-up for the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report shows that רבי allowed himself some small physical actions during תפלה, like feeling his clothing and yawning. But he set limits: he did not wrap himself during prayer, and he covered his open mouth out of respect. These details become the target of the coming objection.

keyTerms.meaning: Feels around, touches with his hand
Wraps himself (in his garment or טלית)

phrases.english: And he would feel around in his garment,
phrases.notes: This continues the earlier report: if a louse bothered him, he would feel for it through his clothing.

phrases.english: but he would not wrap himself.
phrases.notes: If his garment slipped off during prayer, he would not stop to wrap himself again.

phrases.english: And when he would yawn,
he would place his hand on his chin.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְמַשְׁמֵשׁ בְּבִגְדוֹ, אֲבָל לֹא הָיָה מִתְעַטֵּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the report about רבי that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During תפלה רבי would feel his garment, would not wrap himself, and covered his mouth when yawning.

steps.title: A ברייתא harshly criticizes noises and bodily actions during prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that condemns loud prayer, burping, yawning, sneezing and spitting during תפלה. This seems to contradict what רבי did.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: One who makes his voice heard in his prayer is one of those with little faith. One who raises his voice in his prayer is one of the false prophets. One who burps or yawns is one of the arrogant. One who sneezes during his prayer, it is a bad sign for him. Some say: it shows that he is disgusting. One who spits during his prayer is like someone who spits in front of the king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that criticizes many physical actions during תפלה. The point is to challenge the report about רבי, who did some of these things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists burping, yawning, sneezing and spitting as serious faults during תפלה. But the report says רבי did these things himself. So how could a great צדיק like רבי behave in a way the ברייתא condemns? The lines about the voice are part of the same ברייתא, quoted together with the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא or other source)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מִתְעַטֵּף (wraps himself, in step 1) with מִתְעַטֵּשׁ (sneezes, here). They look almost the same but mean completely different things.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who makes his voice heard in his prayer
— he is one of those with little faith.
One who raises his voice in his prayer
he is one of the false prophets.
One who burps and yawns —
he is one of the arrogant.
One who sneezes in his prayer — it is a bad sign for him.
And some say: it is clear that he is disgusting.
One who spits in his prayer —
it is as if he spat in front of the king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the report about רבי's conduct with a ברייתא that condemns that kind of conduct.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי burped, yawned, sneezed and spat during תפלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls these actions arrogant, a bad sign, or disrespectful to the King. So how could רבי have done them?

steps.title: Burping and yawning: by accident versus on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the burping and yawning contradiction: רבי could not help it, while the ברייתא condemns someone who does it on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that burping and yawning is not a problem: here it was not on purpose, and here it was on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers part of the challenge. Burping and yawning are fine when you cannot help it; the ברייתא only condemns doing them on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources are talking about different situations. רבי burped and yawned because he could not control it (אונס), which is allowed. The ברייתא condemns someone who does it on purpose (רצון), which shows arrogance.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, granted (the גמרא is about to show that one part still does not work)
On purpose, by his own choice

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a basic rule for תפלה: a bodily reaction you cannot control is not counted as disrespect, but doing it on purpose is.

phrases.english: Granted, burping and yawning is not difficult:
here it is against his will, here it is on purpose.
phrases.notes: The first "here" is רבי's case; the second "here" is the ברייתא's case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the part of the objection that is about burping and yawning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: by accident versus on purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burping and yawning during תפלה are always condemned, so רבי's behavior contradicts the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי did it by accident, which is allowed; the ברייתא condemns doing it on purpose.

steps.title: The sneezing contradiction is still a problem
steps.stepSummary: The same answer does not work for sneezing, so the contradiction between רבי's sneezing and the ברייתא's sneezing remains difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: But sneezing against sneezing is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer from step 3 does not fix the sneezing problem. The contradiction is still open, and the גמרא will need to answer it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sneezing is almost always something a person cannot help. So the ברייתא, which calls sneezing a bad sign, must also be talking about an accidental sneeze. That means the "by accident versus on purpose" answer cannot split the two sources, and רבי's sneezing still seems to clash with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Against (the case of) sneezing; short for עַל מִתְעַטֵּשׁ
It is difficult, a problem remains

phrases.english: But sneezing against sneezing is difficult!
phrases.notes: This compares the sneezing in רבי's report with the sneezing the ברייתא calls a bad sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer of step 3 cannot handle the sneezing part of the objection.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי sneezed during תפלה, set against the ברייתא's statement that sneezing during prayer is a bad sign.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sneezing is naturally not on purpose, so the split between accident and choice does not apply. The two sources still contradict each other.

steps.title: Sneezing from above versus from below
steps.stepSummary: The sneezing contradiction is resolved: רבי sneezed through his nose, while the ברייתא condemns passing wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sneezing against sneezing is also not a problem. One case is a sneeze from above, and the other is a 'sneeze' from below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question left open in Step 4. It says the two sources are talking about two different kinds of 'sneezing.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's sneeze was a normal sneeze from the nose (from above). The ברייתא's bad sign is about passing wind (from below). So they are not talking about the same thing, and the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: In this line 'below' means a bodily sound from below, not 'down here on earth.' In the next step the same words get a different meaning.

phrases.english: Sneezing against sneezing is also not difficult:
here, it is from above;
phrases.notes: This is רבי's case: an ordinary sneeze through the nose.

phrases.english: here, it is from below.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא's case: passing wind, which is a bad sign during prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the open difficulty about sneezing from Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the same word describes two different bodily actions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources are about the same kind of sneeze, so רבי did something the ברייתא condemns.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי sneezed from the nose, which is fine. The ברייתא condemns passing wind.

steps.title: רב זירא: sneezing in prayer is a good sign
steps.stepSummary: רב זירא's teaching supports the answer: sneezing through the nose during תפלה is actually a good sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב זירא said: I picked up this teaching in passing at the school of רב המנונא, and to me it is worth as much as all my learning. If someone sneezes during his prayer, it is a good sign for him. Just as they give him relief below, so they give him relief above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer. רב זירא teaches that a nose-sneeze during prayer is a good sign, so רבי's sneezing was nothing bad at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 5 said sneezing from above is acceptable. רב זירא goes further and calls it a good sign. The bodily relief a person feels down here is a hint that Heaven is pleased with his prayer up above.

keyTerms.meaning: It was absorbed by me; I picked it up in passing

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns רבי's sneezing from something that only needs excusing into something positive.

phrases.english: As Rav Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִילְּתָא אִבַּלְעָא לִי בֵּי רַב הַמְנוּנָא
phrases.english: This matter I picked up in passing at the school of Rav Hamnuna,
phrases.notes: Literally 'was swallowed by me.' He heard it on the side, without formally studying it.

phrases.english: and it weighs for me as much as all my learning:
One who sneezes during his prayer, it is a good sign for him.

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁעוֹשִׂים לוֹ נַחַת רוּחַ מִלְּמַטָּה,
phrases.english: Just as they give him relief below,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ עוֹשִׂים לוֹ נַחַת רוּחַ מִלְּמַעְלָה.
phrases.english: so they give him relief from above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the answer of Step 5 by showing that a nose-sneeze in prayer is good.
steps.raayaObject: That sneezing from above (the nose) during prayer is not condemned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב זירא's teaching from the school of רב המנונא.

steps.title: The spitting contradiction remains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the last contradiction: רבי spat during prayer, but the ברייתא condemns spitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: But spitting against spitting is still a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the spitting contradiction has not been solved yet. This line sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither earlier answer works for spitting. 'He couldn't help it' does not fit, and spitting has no 'above versus below' split. So רבי's spitting still seems to clash with the ברייתא.

phrases.english: But spitting against spitting is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After sneezing is settled, moves to the last item still unresolved.
steps.kashyaTarget: The contradiction between רבי's spitting and the ברייתא's ban on spitting in prayer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answers given for burping, yawning and sneezing cannot be applied to spitting.

steps.title: Spitting the respectful way, following רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Spitting is acceptable if it is done discreetly into one's garment, as רב יהודה teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Spitting against spitting is also not a problem. It can be done the way רב יהודה said. רב יהודה said: If someone is standing in prayer and saliva comes into his mouth, he soaks it into his garment. If it is a nice garment, he soaks it into his head covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the spitting contradiction. רבי spat in a discreet, respectful way, while the ברייתא condemns spitting out openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is against spitting out in the open during prayer. רב יהודה shows there is a proper way to deal with saliva: absorb it quietly into cloth. רבי must have done it that way, so he did nothing wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: He absorbs it, soaks it in

phrases.english: Spitting against spitting is also not difficult:
it is possible to do it like Rav Yehuda.
As Rav Yehuda said:
If one was standing in prayer
and saliva came to him,
he absorbs it into his garment.
And if it is a fine garment,
he absorbs it into his head covering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָק אַרָק נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא, אֶפְשָׁר כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the spitting difficulty of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by method: discreet absorbing versus open spitting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any spitting during prayer is like spitting before the King, so רבי did wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Spitting discreetly into a cloth is allowed. Only open spitting is condemned.
steps.whatToRemember: All four contradictions are now settled. Burping and yawning: רבי couldn't help it. Sneezing: his was from the nose. Spitting: he absorbed it discreetly, like רב יהודה says.

steps.title: רב אשי questions רבינא's way of spitting
steps.stepSummary: A story: רבינא, standing behind רב אשי, spat behind himself during prayer, and רב אשי asked why he did not follow רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא was standing behind רב אשי. Saliva came into רבינא's mouth, and he spat it out behind him. רב אשי said to him: Doesn't the Master agree with רב יהודה's teaching that one should absorb it into his head covering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רב יהודה's rule in real life. רב אשי asks why רבינא spat out behind him instead of using his head covering, and this sets up רבינא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned the proper method from רב יהודה. Here רבינא seems to do something else, so רב אשי asks why. The question tests whether רב יהודה's method is a must for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: He threw it, spat it out
Master, a respectful way to address a teacher

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא הֲוָה קָאֵי אֲחוֹרֵי רַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Ravina was standing behind Rav Ashi.
Saliva came to him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' here is רבינא, the one standing behind his teacher.

phrases.english: and he spat it out behind him.
He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Does the Master not hold of this teaching of Rav Yehuda,
that he absorbs it into his head covering?

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא הֲוָה קָאֵי אֲחוֹרֵי רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רב יהודה's rule from Step 8 being put to the test in a real case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבינא did not follow רב יהודה's method of absorbing the spit.

steps.title: רבינא: I am too sensitive
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that he is too sensitive to keep spit in his head covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am a delicate person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רב אשי. He is personally too sensitive to have saliva in his head covering, so he spat behind him instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא does not reject רב יהודה's rule. He explains that for someone as sensitive as he is, keeping spit in his clothing would bother him and ruin his concentration. So for him, spitting behind himself was the better choice.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am delicate-minded.
phrases.notes: He means that knowing the spit was in his head covering would disgust him and distract him from praying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question from Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person who is sensitive may spit behind himself instead of absorbing it in cloth.

steps.title: רב הונא limits the rule against praying aloud
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא's first item. רב הונא says praying aloud is condemned only for someone who can concentrate quietly.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who makes his voice heard in his prayer is one of those with little faith. רב הונא said: They only taught this about someone who can concentrate while whispering. But if he cannot concentrate while whispering, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first line of the ברייתא, about praying out loud. רב הונא explains that this rule does not apply to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sounds absolute: praying out loud shows weak faith, as if God can't hear a whisper. רב הונא limits it to someone who could focus quietly. If a person can only concentrate by saying the words aloud, he may do so.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes his voice heard
They only taught this in the case of...
To focus his heart; to concentrate

phrases.english: One who makes his voice heard in his prayer
is one of those of little faith.
Rav Huna said: They only taught this

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְכַוֵּון אֶת לִבּוֹ בְּלַחַשׁ,
phrases.english: where he is able to concentrate while whispering;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין יָכוֹל לְכַוֵּון אֶת לִבּוֹ בְּלַחַשׁ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: but if he cannot concentrate while whispering, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bodily-actions discussion and returns to the ברייתא's first item, praying aloud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praying aloud is condemned only for someone who can concentrate quietly. Someone who cannot may pray aloud.

steps.title: The allowance applies only when praying alone
steps.stepSummary: Praying aloud is allowed only for someone praying alone. In a congregation it would disturb others.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to someone praying alone. But in a congregation, he will come to disturb the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to רב הונא's allowance. Someone who needs to pray aloud may do so only when he is by himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא allowed praying aloud for someone who cannot concentrate otherwise. Now we learn that this is only when he is alone. With a group, his voice would disturb the others' prayers, so it is not allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Praying aloud: forbidden if you can focus quietly. Allowed if you can't, but only when you are alone and not in a congregation.

phrases.english: And this applies only to an individual,
but in a congregation,
he will come to disturb the congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב הונא's allowance from Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The allowance to pray aloud is only for someone praying alone, because in a congregation it disturbs others.

steps.title: רבי אבא avoids רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. רבי אבא avoids his teacher רב יהודה because he wants to move to ארץ ישראל, and רב יהודה holds that this breaks a מצוות עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא was avoiding רב יהודה, because he wanted to go up to ארץ ישראל. For רב יהודה said: Anyone who goes up from בבל to ארץ ישראל transgresses a positive commandment, as it says: 'They shall be brought to Babylon, and there they shall be, until the day I remember them, says ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. It explains why רבי אבא was staying away from his teacher רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה learns from a פסוק in ירמיהו that the Jews in בבל must stay there until God brings them back. So leaving בבל for ארץ ישראל counts as breaking a positive commandment. רבי אבא wanted to go anyway, so he avoided facing his teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַבָּא הֲוָה קָא מִשְׁתְּמִיט מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba was avoiding Rav Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה קָא בָּעֵי לְמִיסַּק לְאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: because he wanted to go up to Eretz Yisrael,
phrases.notes: The one who wanted to go up is רבי אבא, not רב יהודה.

phrases.english: for Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעוֹלֶה מִבָּבֶל לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל — עוֹבֵר בַּעֲשֵׂה,
phrases.english: Anyone who goes up from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael transgresses a positive commandment,
as it is said:
"They shall be brought to Babylonia, and there they shall be,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 27:22

phrases.aramaic: עַד יוֹם פׇּקְדִי אוֹתָם נְאֻם ה׳״.
phrases.english: until the day I remember them, says the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא הֲוָה קָא מִשְׁתְּמִיט מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, unconnected to the prayer-behavior discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה holds that moving from בבל to ארץ ישראל transgresses a positive commandment, based on ירמיהו.

steps.title: Rabbi Abba's plan before leaving
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא decides to hear one more teaching from רב יהודה before he leaves for ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I will go and hear something from him at the gathering hall, and then I will leave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא makes a plan. He will quietly hear one more teaching from רב יהודה and then go. This sets up the rest of the story, which continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even while avoiding his teacher, רבי אבא still wants to learn Torah from him. He plans to listen without being noticed at the place where the חכמים gather, and only then leave בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: The gathering hall where the חכמים meet

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: אֵיזִיל וְאֶשְׁמַע מִינֵּיהּ מִילְּתָא מִבֵּית וַועֲדָא,
phrases.english: He said: I will go and hear something from him at the gathering hall,
and afterward I will leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: אֵיזִיל וְאֶשְׁמַע מִינֵּיהּ מִילְּתָא מִבֵּית וַועֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רבי אבא story from Step 13 and sets up what he will hear next.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבא plans to hear one more teaching from רב יהודה before leaving for ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Passing wind during תפילה: wait and continue
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא hears the תנא reciting a ברייתא before רב יהודה. Someone who passes wind during תפילה waits until the smell is gone and then goes back to praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and found the תנא who was reciting before רב יהודה: If someone was standing in תפילה and passed wind, he waits until the smell goes away, and then he goes back and prays.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא went into the study hall, as he planned in step 14. He hears a ברייתא about a person who passes wind in the middle of תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the 'one more teaching' רבי אבא wanted to hear. The rule is simple: a smell interrupts תפילה, so the person stops and waits until the air is clear. Then he continues praying.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a person whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות in the study hall
Literally 'sneezed.' Here it is a polite way of saying he passed wind

steps.confusionAlert: 'Sneezed' here does not mean a normal sneeze through the nose. It is a polite way of saying passing wind, so do not picture a nose sneeze.

phrases.english: He went and found the tanna
who was reciting before Rav Yehuda:
If one was standing in prayer and 'sneezed' (passed wind),
he waits until the smell is gone
and goes back and prays.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְתַנָּא דְּקָתָנֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out רבי אבא's plan from step 14 to hear one more teaching before leaving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who passes wind during תפילה waits until the smell is gone and then continues praying.

steps.title: A longer version: step back and say a special prayer
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the ruling. The person steps back ארבע אמות, waits for the smell to go away, says a short humble prayer, and then continues from where he stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: If someone was standing in תפילה and needed to pass wind, he moves back four אמות, passes wind, and waits until the smell is gone. Then he returns to pray and says: 'Master of the world, You made us with many openings and hollows. Our shame in life is known to You, and in the end we become maggots and worms.' Then he starts from where he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, more detailed version of the same rule. Here the person moves away first and says a short prayer before continuing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version only said 'wait and continue.' This version adds three things: he moves away ארבע אמות before passing wind, he says a humble prayer about how weak the human body is, and he picks up exactly where he stopped. The prayer is a way of asking ה׳ to understand our human weakness.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces a second version of a teaching
Many openings and many hollows in the body
He starts again from the place where he stopped

phrases.english: Some say:
If one was standing in prayer and needed to 'sneeze' (pass wind),
he moves back four cubits,
passes wind, and waits until the smell is gone,
and goes back to pray, and says:
'Master of the world, You formed us
with many openings and many hollows;
it is revealed and known before You
our disgrace and our shame in our lives
and in our end, maggots and worms,'
and he begins from the place where he stopped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, fuller version of the ruling in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who feels he needs to pass wind moves back four אמות, waits for the smell to clear, says the prayer 'רבונו של עולם', and continues from where he stopped.

steps.title: רבי אבא: this teaching alone was worth it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says that even if he had come only to hear this one teaching, it would have been enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: If I had come only to hear this one thing, it would have been enough for me.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רבי אבא ends here. He says that this one teaching made his visit worthwhile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 רבי אבא went to hear one last teaching before moving to ארץ ישראל. He got a practical rule that teaches care and humility in תפילה, and he felt fully satisfied.

keyTerms.meaning: If I had come only for this
It would have been enough for me

steps.whatToRemember: The rules about passing wind during תפילה come up while telling the story of רבי אבא. There are two versions: wait and continue, or step back ארבע אמות, say 'רבונו של עולם', and continue from where you stopped.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי אבא, reacting to what he just heard.

phrases.english: If I had come only
to hear this thing, it would have been enough for me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ לֹא בָּאתִי אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוֹעַ דָּבָר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the רבי אבא story with his reaction to the teaching from steps 15–16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אבא valued this teaching about care in תפילה so much that it alone made his visit worthwhile.

steps.title: Saying קריאת שמע while covered in bed
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: a person sleeping under his garment who cannot stick his head out because of the cold makes a divider with the garment at his neck and says קריאת שמע. יש אומרים: the divider must be at his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone was sleeping in his garment and cannot take his head out because of the cold, he presses his garment against his neck to make a divider and reads קריאת שמע. Some say: at his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about saying קריאת שמע in bed without clothes, covered only by a garment. There are two opinions about where the divider has to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His head is under the same garment as his uncovered body, so he must separate himself from his ערוה before saying קריאת שמע. The תנא קמא says a divider at the neck is enough, because it separates the mouth from the ערוה. The יש אומרים require the divider lower down, at the heart.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: introduces a ברייתא
And some say: a second opinion

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If one was sleeping in his garment,
phrases.notes: The case is someone with no clothes on, covered only by this garment.

phrases.english: and he cannot take his head out
because of the cold,
he makes a divider with his garment at his neck,
and reads the Shema.
And some say: at his heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא, moving from תפילה to modesty during קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: a divider at the neck is enough to say קריאת שמע. יש אומרים: the divider must be at the heart.

steps.title: Challenge: the heart still sees the ערוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to the תנא קמא, the divider is only at the neck, so his heart 'sees' the ערוה. Why is that allowed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the first תנא, his heart sees the ערוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא. With the divider only at the neck, nothing separates his heart from his ערוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes the heart must also be separated from the ערוה during קריאת שמע, just as the mouth is. If so, a divider at the neck should not be enough, and the יש אומרים would be right.

keyTerms.meaning: The first תנא: the first opinion in the ברייתא
His heart 'sees' the ערוה: nothing separates his heart from his uncovered body

phrases.english: And according to the first tanna,
his heart sees the nakedness!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא הֲרֵי לִבּוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תנא קמא's ruling in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's ruling that a divider at the neck is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A divider at the neck leaves the heart and the ערוה with nothing between them, which seems to be forbidden.

steps.title: The תנא קמא holds the heart seeing the ערוה is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא holds it is permitted for the heart to 'see' the ערוה. Only the mouth must be separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that if his heart sees the ערוה, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The תנא קמא simply holds that the heart seeing the ערוה is not a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed everyone agrees the heart must be separated. The answer shows this is exactly what the two opinions argue about. The תנא קמא allows it, so he only needs a divider at the neck to separate the mouth. The יש אומרים forbid it, so they require the divider at the heart.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא and the יש אומרים disagree about whether the heart may 'see' the ערוה during קריאת שמע. The תנא קמא allows it and only requires separating the mouth, at the neck. The יש אומרים require a divider at the heart.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer turns a question into the real point of the argument: both sides agree the mouth must be separated, and they disagree only about the heart.

phrases.english: He holds that when his heart sees the nakedness,
it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר לִבּוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the underlying disagreement: the תנא קמא does not accept the assumption behind the challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought everyone agrees the heart may not 'see' the ערוה, so a divider at the neck should not be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא holds the heart seeing the ערוה is permitted, so a divider at the neck, which separates the mouth, is enough.

steps.title: Covering the mouth to say שמע in filthy alleys
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes רבי יוחנן: a person walking through filthy alleys puts his hand over his mouth and says קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone was walking through filthy alleys, he puts his hand over his mouth and says קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling: walking through a filthy alley does not stop you from saying קריאת שמע, as long as you cover your mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps just before this said the mouth is the main thing that must be separated from something improper. This ruling goes further: a hand over the mouth is enough, even in a place full of filth.

keyTerms.meaning: Filthy alleys, dirtied with human waste
He puts his hand over his mouth

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
If one was walking in filthy alleyways,
he places his hand over his mouth
and recites Shema.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of what must be separated from filth or nakedness during קריאת שמע, now for a person walking through filth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Walking in filthy alleys, one covers his mouth with his hand and may say קריאת שמע.

steps.title: רב חסדא strongly rejects the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא swears he would not obey this ruling even if רבי יוחנן had said it to him in person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: By God! Even if רבי יוחנן had told it to me with his own mouth, I would not listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא completely rejects the ruling from the last step and says he would never follow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא does not argue about the wording. He rejects the ruling itself, because he thinks saying שמע in a filthy place is not allowed even with a hand over the mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: I would not listen to him

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said to him: By God!

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַמְרָהּ לִי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּפוּמֵּיהּ —
phrases.english: Even if Rabbi Yoḥanan had said it to me with his own mouth,
I would not have obeyed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the ruling of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one may say שמע in filthy alleys while covering his mouth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A hand over the mouth is not enough to allow saying שמע in a filthy place. רב חסדא gives no source, only a firm refusal.

steps.title: Second version: the ruling in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: Some report the same ruling through רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, with the same strong rejection from רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: if someone was walking through filthy alleys, he puts his hand over his mouth and says קריאת שמע. רב חסדא said: By God! Even if רבי יהושע בן לוי had told it to me with his own mouth, I would not listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of the same ruling and the same reaction. Only the names are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling and רב חסדא's rejection are word-for-word the same. What changes is who said it: רבה בר בר חנה quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי, instead of רב הונא quoting רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (a second version of the report)
An אמורא who passes on teachings of earlier sages

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling. It is the same ruling told in other people's names, so the questions that come next can be aimed at either version.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
If one was walking in filthy alleyways,

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ עַל פִּיו וְקוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע.
phrases.english: he places his hand over his mouth and recites Shema.
Rav Ḥisda said to him: By God!

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַמְרָהּ לִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי בְּפוּמֵּיהּ —
phrases.english: Even if Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi had said it to me with his own mouth,
I would not have obeyed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second report of steps 21 and 22, with different names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same ruling as step 21, said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, and רב חסדא rejects it the same way.

steps.title: Did רב הונא really say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from his own teaching that a תלמיד חכם may not stand in a filthy place, because he cannot help thinking Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב הונא really say this? But רב הונא said: a תלמיד חכם is not allowed to stand in a filthy place, because he cannot stand there without thinking about Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב הונא seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא forbids a scholar even to stand in filth, because he will end up thinking Torah thoughts there. If just thinking is a problem, saying שמע out loud should be even worse. So how could he report that one may say שמע in filthy alleys?

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (opens a contradiction)
Thinking about Torah in one's mind

phrases.english: And did Rav Huna really say this?
But didn't Rav Huna say:
A Torah scholar is forbidden
to stand in a place of filth
because it is impossible for him to stand
without thinking about Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ruling of step 21 and tests it against another teaching of רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's report that one may say שמע in filthy alleys.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even thinking Torah in filth is forbidden, then saying שמע out loud must be forbidden too.

steps.title: Standing versus walking
steps.stepSummary: The two teachings do not clash. Standing in filth is forbidden, but walking through it is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a problem. Here he is standing, and here he is walking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles רב הונא's two teachings by showing they are about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on a scholar being in a filthy place is for someone standing there. The permission to say שמע with a covered mouth is for someone just walking through. Passing through is treated more leniently than staying.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

phrases.english: It is not difficult: here it is when standing,
here it is when walking.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן בְּעוֹמֵד, כָּאן בִּמְהַלֵּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like רב הונא forbade any Torah, even thinking, in a filthy place.
steps.terutzMaskana: His ban is only for standing there. Walking through allows שמע with a covered mouth.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from his teaching that one may think Torah anywhere except a bathhouse or bathroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: you may think about Torah anywhere, except in a bathhouse and a bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא tests the other half of the report: does the ruling fit what רבי יוחנן said elsewhere?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן forbids even thinking about Torah in a bathroom, which is a place of filth. So how could he allow saying שמע out loud in a filthy alley?

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yoḥanan really say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabba bar bar Ḥana say in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכָל מָקוֹם מוּתָּר לְהַרְהֵר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Everywhere it is permitted to think about matters of Torah,
except the bathhouse and the bathroom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like step 24, but now aimed at רבי יוחנן, the original source of the ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling allowing שמע in filthy alleys.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even thinking Torah is forbidden in a bathroom, then saying שמע aloud in a filthy place must be forbidden too.

steps.title: Suggesting the same standing-versus-walking answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers the answer it used for רב הונא: maybe רבי יוחנן's ban is for standing, and his permission is for walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: here too, one case is about standing and the other is about walking —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer, but it is only a setup. The very next step will push it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This copies the answer from step 25 and applies it to רבי יוחנן. The words וכי תימא tell us the גמרא is raising a possible answer so it can test it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (introduces a suggested answer)

phrases.english: And if you say:
Here too, here it is when standing,
and here it is when walking —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכָא נָמֵי כָּאן בְּעוֹמֵד כָּאן בִּמְהַלֵּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer step 26 using the same split as step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggested split between cases (standing versus walking), not yet accepted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's two teachings seem to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe the bathroom ban is for standing and the alley permission is for walking. This is tested and rejected next.

steps.title: The story of רבי אבהו stopping שמע in a filthy alley
steps.stepSummary: The answer is pushed away by a story. רבי אבהו stopped saying שמע while walking through a filthy alley, and רבי יוחנן only told him where to start again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי אבהו was walking behind רבי יוחנן and saying קריאת שמע. When he reached filthy alleys, he went quiet. He said to רבי יוחנן: Where should I go back to? רבי יוחנן said to him: If you paused long enough to finish all of it, go back to the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the standing-versus-walking answer by telling a story that shows רבי יוחנן also stops שמע while walking through filth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו was walking, not standing, and he still stopped saying שמע in the filthy alley. רבי יוחנן did not tell him he could have continued with his hand over his mouth. He only answered where to restart, so he seems to agree that one should stop. That means the walking case cannot explain the ruling in רבי יוחנן's name.

keyTerms.meaning: To where should I go back?

keyTerms.term: אִם שָׁהִיתָ כְּדֵי לִגְמוֹר אֶת כּוּלָּהּ
keyTerms.meaning: If you paused as long as it takes to finish the whole thing

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's two teachings fit together by splitting standing from walking. The story of רבי אבהו seems to show that the split cannot work for רבי יוחנן, but the next step pushes this proof away.
steps.confusionAlert: The story never says outright that רבי יוחנן approved of stopping. The point comes from what he did not say: he did not correct רבי אבהו, he only answered where to restart.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story also teaches a separate rule: if you stop in the middle of שמע for as long as it takes to say all of it, you go back to the beginning.

phrases.aramaic: אִינִי, וְהָא רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל
phrases.english: Is that so? But Rabbi Abbahu was walking
behind Rabbi Yoḥanan
and was reciting Shema.
When he reached filthy alleyways, he fell silent.
He said to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
To where should I return?
phrases.notes: He means: at what point in שמע should I pick up again, now that we're out of the alley?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם שָׁהִיתָ כְּדֵי לִגְמוֹר אֶת כּוּלָּהּ —
phrases.english: He said to him: If you paused long enough to finish all of it,
go back to the beginning!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי, וְהָא רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer of step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבי יוחנן allows שמע while walking through filth.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A story shows רבי יוחנן going along with stopping שמע even while walking, so the walking case does not explain his ruling.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was answering by רבי אבהו's view
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the story is pushed away. רבי יוחנן did not personally hold that one must stop. He only told רבי אבהו what to do according to רבי אבהו's own opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי יוחנן meant: 'I myself don't hold that you needed to stop. But since you do hold that, here is the rule for you: if you paused long enough to finish the whole שמע, go back to the beginning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the proof from the story of רבי אבהו. It explains that רבי יוחנן's advice does not show what רבי יוחנן himself held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28, the story seemed to show that רבי יוחנן agreed one must stop reciting even while walking. Now the גמרא says רבי יוחנן was only answering by רבי אבהו's opinion, not his own. So the earlier answer, that walking is different from standing, can stand again.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant to tell him
I myself do not hold this
He paused long enough to finish the whole thing

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the story as רבי יוחנן's own ruling. He was answering a question asked from רבי אבהו's point of view.

phrases.english: This is what he said to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יוחנן, talking to רבי אבהו from the story in step 28.

phrases.english: I myself do not hold this,
but for you, since you do hold it,

phrases.aramaic: אִם שָׁהִיתָ כְּדֵי לִגְמוֹר אֶת כּוּלָּהּ
phrases.english: if you paused long enough to finish all of it,
phrases.notes: "All of it" means the whole קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: go back to the beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes away the story-based rejection in step 28, so the answer from step 27 is restored.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי יוחנן's reply to רבי אבהו
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reply followed רבי אבהו's opinion, not רבי יוחנן's own, so it tells us nothing about what רבי יוחנן held.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב הונא and רבי יוחנן can be explained by the standing-versus-walking split. The story of רבי אבהו does not disprove it, because רבי יוחנן was answering by רבי אבהו's own opinion. Along the way we learn: if you pause in שמע long enough to finish all of it, you go back to the beginning.

steps.title: A ברייתא that backs רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that each side has a ברייתא supporting it. It then quotes the one for רב הונא: someone walking in filthy alleys covers his mouth and recites שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a ברייתא that agrees with רב הונא, and there is a ברייתא that agrees with רב חסדא. The one that agrees with רב הונא says: someone walking in filthy alleys puts his hand over his mouth and recites קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up support for both sides of the רב הונא and רב חסדא disagreement. It then quotes the ברייתא that backs רב הונא's lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening line is a setup that promises two sources, one for each side. The first ברייתא allows reciting שמע while walking through filth, as long as he covers his mouth. That matches רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught that agrees with him
He places his hand over his mouth

phrases.english: A baraita is taught that agrees with Rav Huna,
and a baraita is taught that agrees with Rav Chisda.
The one that agrees with Rav Huna:
One who walks in filthy alleyways
places his hand over his mouth
and recites Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוחנן discussion and brings sources for the basic disagreement.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that one may recite שמע while walking in filthy alleys
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: cover the mouth and recite

steps.title: A ברייתא that backs רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא forbids reciting שמע while walking in filthy alleys. It adds that if he was already in the middle of reciting, he must stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one that agrees with רב חסדא says: someone walking in filthy alleys may not recite קריאת שמע. Not only that, but if he was already reciting when he got there, he stops.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second ברייתא, which supports רב חסדא's strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא goes further than simply forbidding him to begin. Even someone already in the middle of שמע has to stop when he reaches the filthy place. That fits רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: He was in the middle of reciting as he came

steps.whatToRemember: There are ברייתות on both sides. One allows reciting with a covered mouth, like רב הונא. The other forbids it and even requires stopping in the middle, like רב חסדא.

phrases.english: The one that agrees with Rav Chisda:
If he was walking in filthy alleyways,
he may not recite Shema,
and not only that, but
if he was in the middle of reciting as he came, he stops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Delivers the second source promised in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's view that one may not recite שמע in filthy alleys
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: do not recite, and stop if already reciting

steps.title: What if he did not stop?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what we say about someone who kept reciting in the filthy alley instead of stopping.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not stop, what then?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next answers. What is the status of someone who kept reciting in a filthy place?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said he must stop, but it did not say what happens if he doesn't. The answers in the next steps describe how wrong his act is.

keyTerms.meaning: If he did not stop, what is the law?

phrases.english: If he did not stop, what then?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the ruling in רב חסדא's ברייתא that he must stop.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The status of someone who kept reciting שמע in a filthy place

steps.title: רבי מיאשה: laws that are not good
steps.stepSummary: רבי מיאשה, grandson of רבי יהושע בן לוי, applies a פסוק about laws that bring no life to someone who did not stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מיאשה, the grandson of רבי יהושע בן לוי, said: about him the פסוק says, 'And I also gave them laws that are not good, and rules they cannot live by.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer uses a פסוק to show that this person did wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He meant to do a מצוה by saying שמע. But because he said it in a filthy place, his act became something bad instead of something that gives life.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meyasha said,

phrases.aramaic: בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: the grandson of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
About him the verse says:
"And I also gave them
laws that are not good
and rules they cannot live by."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 20:25

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מְיָאשָׁה בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He did wrong; the פסוק about laws that are not good applies to him.

steps.title: Two more פסוקים: רב אסי and רב אדא בר אהבה
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי and רב אדא בר אהבה each bring a different פסוק that describes someone who kept reciting in filth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said the source is: 'Woe to those who pull sin along with ropes of nothing.' רב אדא בר אהבה said it comes from here: 'For he has scorned the word of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two more אמוראים give other פסוקים for the same idea. Each one shows that this person acted wrongly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי's פסוק describes someone who brings sin on himself for nothing. רב אדא בר אהבה's פסוק calls it scorning the word of ה׳, because he said holy words in a dirty place.

keyTerms.meaning: He scorned the word of ה׳

steps.whatToRemember: Someone who keeps reciting שמע in a filthy place does not get credit for a מצוה. Three פסוקים describe him as doing something wrong, even as scorning the word of ה׳.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
"Woe to those who pull sin along with ropes of nothing."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 5:18

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said, from here:
"For he has scorned the word of the Lord."
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:31

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives other פסוקים for the same answer that רבי מיאשה gave.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He brings sin on himself for nothing, and he scorns the word of ה׳.

steps.title: What reward does the one who stopped get?
steps.stepSummary: After hearing what happens to someone who kept reading in filth, the גמרא asks about the opposite person, the one who stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he did stop, what is his reward?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the question from the last steps. Now it asks about the person who did the right thing and stopped. This line sets up רבי אבהו's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 33-34 gave פסוקים describing the person who kept reading in a filthy place. Now the גמרא looks at the good side: the person who stopped reading out of respect for the words of שמע.

phrases.english: And if he stopped, what is his reward?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror of step 32's question: that step asked about the one who did not stop, and this one asks about the one who did.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reward the person gets for stopping שמע in a filthy place.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: he earns a long life
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו applies the פסוק 'through this matter you will prolong your days' to the person who stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: About him the פסוק says, 'And through this thing you will lengthen your days.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question. He says the person who stopped is rewarded with a long life, and he brings a פסוק to show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier speakers gave harsh פסוקים for the person who kept reading in filth. רבי אבהו gives a positive one for the person who stopped. Being careful about where you say holy words earns long life.
steps.whatToRemember: The person who keeps reading שמע in filth is criticized with harsh פסוקים. The person who stops gets a blessing of long life.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
About him the verse says:
"And through this thing you will lengthen your days."
phrases.notes: דברים 32:47

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The person who stops earns long life, based on the פסוק in דברים 32:47.

steps.title: רב הונא: a garment tied around the waist is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a person whose garment is tied around his waist may say קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If his garment was tied around his waist, he may say קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here. רב הונא says that a person with his garment tied around his waist is allowed to say שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that the lower body is covered by the tied garment, even if the upper body is not. רב הונא rules that this is enough covering to say שמע.
steps.confusionAlert: Here טלית means any outer garment or wrap, not the טלית with ציצית that we wear for תפילה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה טַלִּיתוֹ חֲגוּרָה לוֹ עַל מׇתְנָיו —
phrases.english: If his garment was tied around his waist,
he is permitted to recite קריאת שמע.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא הָיְתָה טַלִּיתוֹ חֲגוּרָה לוֹ עַל מׇתְנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the filthy-alley discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A garment tied around the waist is enough covering to say קריאת שמע.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule as רב הונא and adds that it applies to a garment made of any material: cloth, leather or sack.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: If his garment of cloth, leather or sackcloth was tied around his waist, he may say קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב הונא. This gives his ruling support from an earlier source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees with רב הונא's ruling. It also tells us something new: the material of the garment does not matter. Cloth, leather and sackcloth all work, as long as the garment is tied around the waist.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא and the ברייתא agree: a garment of any material tied around the waist is enough to allow saying שמע.

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
If his garment, of cloth
or of leather or of sackcloth,
was tied around his waist,
he is permitted to recite קריאת שמע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of רב הונא in step 37.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that a garment tied around the waist is enough to say שמע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same ruling, applied to garments of any material.
